abstract: Quarantine pests pose major threats to global biosafety, agriculture, and biodiversity. However, information of their regulatory status, biology, distribution, and molecular resources remains fragmented across multiple sources, which hinders the in-depth analysis of quarantine pests. Here, we present the Quarantine Pest Database (QPD, https://qpests.insect-genome.com), an open-access resource that integrates global regulations with biological knowledge, multi-omics sequences, and distribution of quarantine pests. QPD integrates official quarantine pest lists, complementary phytosanitary notifications, and distribution records of 231 countries and regions, covering 9849 regulated pest taxa, 7666 host plants, 2057 genome assemblies, 4877 transcriptomes, and 1 311 846 DNA barcode sequences. We also provide 21 747 habitat suitability maps for 4350 quarantine pests under historical and future climate conditions. Each pest entry contains the comprehensive information of standardized taxonomy and jurisdiction-specific quarantine status with host associations, distribution records, morphological descriptions, images, literature references, and available omics resources. Moreover, QPD provides interactive browsing and retrieval, DNA barcode finding, global distribution visualization, and model-based habitat suitability maps. To the best of our knowledge, QPD is the first database to integrate global quarantine regulations with biological, molecular, and spatial information of quarantine pests, providing a centralized resource for the community of pest risk assessment and biosecurity research.
